checks: Matched 641c5559a440bf48 §§2–3 (3)–(6). Each cap mass is affine and upper semicontinuous on the compact coupling set because the cap preimage under T is closed. Thus its superlevel feasibility constraint is closed.
If every finite cap list were feasible at vᵧ+ε, compact finite intersection would give feasibility of the full list. Attainment for finite minima converts infeasibility to a strict gap at that level.

The downward hull of the finite cap-mass vectors is nonempty, convex and closed by passing to one weakly convergent subsequence and using each cap’s upper semicontinuity. Its diagonal maximum is a boundary point. A supporting outward vector has all coordinates nonnegative by downward unboundedness, and its positive coordinate sum can be normalized.

A weighted average is at least the least cap mass, giving the opposite dual inequality. At any finite primal optimizer all cap masses are at least v_F and any minimizing weighted average equals v_F, so every positively weighted cap is exactly active and that coupling maximizes the weighted cost.

At the joint maximizer every through-mark cap mass is at least V and the selected weighted maximum is strictly below V+ε. This proves both quantitative inequalities and keeps the approximation at the same mark.
